{{Short description|Category whose objects are measurable spaces and whose morphisms are Markov kernels}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''category of Markov kernels''', often denoted '''Stoch''', is the [[category (category theory)|category]] whose [[object (category theory)|object]]s are [[measurable space]]s and whose [[morphism]]s are [[Markov kernel]]s.
<ref>{{harvp|Lawvere|1962}}</ref><ref>{{harvp|Chentsov|1965}}</ref><ref name="giry">{{harvp|Giry|1982|page=69}}</ref><ref name="fritz">{{harvp|Fritz|2020|pages=19-21}}</ref>
It is analogous to the [[category of sets|category of sets and functions]], but where the [[morphism|arrows]] can be interpreted as being [[stochastic]].

Several variants of this category are used in the literature. For example, one can use subprobability kernels<ref>{{harvp|Panangaden|1999|page=4}}</ref> instead of probability kernels, or more general [[s-finite measure|s-finite]] kernels.<ref>{{harvp|Kallenberg|2017}}</ref>
Also, one can take as morphisms [[equivalence class]]es of Markov kernels under [[almost surely|almost sure equality]];<ref name="krn">{{harvp|Dahlqvist|Danos|Garnier|Silva|2018|page=3}}</ref> see below.

== Definition ==

Recall that a [[Markov kernel]] between [[measurable space]]s <math>(X,\mathcal{F})</math> and <math>(Y,\mathcal{G})</math> is an assignment <math>k:X\times\mathcal{G}\to\mathbb{R}</math> which is [[measurable function|measurable]] as a function on <math>X</math> and which is a [[probability measure]] on <math>\mathcal{G}</math>.<ref name="fritz"/> We denote its values by <math>k(B|x)</math> for <math>x\in X</math> and <math>B\in\mathcal{G}</math>, which suggests an interpretation as [[conditional probability]].

The category '''Stoch''' has:<ref name="fritz"/>

* As [[object (category theory)|objects]], [[measurable space]]s;
* As [[morphism]]s, [[Markov kernel]]s between them;
* For each measurable space <math>(X,\mathcal{F})</math>, the [[identity morphism]] is given by the kernel 
:<math>
\delta(A|x) = 1_A(x) = \begin{cases}
1 & x\in A ; \\
0 & x\notin A 
\end{cases}
</math>
: for all <math>x\in X</math> and <math>A\in\mathcal{F}</math>;
* Given kernels <math>k:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(Y,\mathcal{G})</math> and <math>h:(Y,\mathcal{G})\to(Z,\mathcal{H})</math>, the composite morphism <math>h\circ k:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(Z,\mathcal{H})</math> is given by 
:<math>
(h\circ k) (C|x) = \int_Y h(C|y) \, k(dy|x)
</math>
: for all <math>x\in X</math> and <math>C\in\mathcal{H}</math>.
This composition formula is sometimes called the [[Chapman-Kolmogorov equation]].<ref name="fritz"/>

This composition is unital, and [[associative]] by the [[monotone convergence theorem]], so that one indeed has a [[category (category theory)|category]].

== Basic properties ==

=== Probability measures ===

The [[terminal object]] of '''Stoch''' is the [[Singleton (mathematics)|one-point space]] <math>1</math>.<ref name="fritz"/> Morphisms in the form <math>1\to X</math> can be equivalently seen as [[probability measure]]s on <math>X</math>, since they correspond to functions <math>1\to PX</math>, i.e. elements of <math>PX</math>.  

Given kernels <math>p:1\to X</math> and <math>k:X\to Y</math>, the composite kernel <math>k\circ p:1\to Y</math> gives the probability measure on <math>Y</math> with values
:<math>
(k\circ p) (B) = \int_X k(B|x)\,p(dx) ,
</math>
for every measurable subset <math>B</math> of <math>Y</math>.<ref name="krn"/>

Given [[probability spaces]] <math>(X,\mathcal{F},p)</math> and <math>(Y,\mathcal{G},q)</math>, a '''measure-preserving Markov kernel''' <math>(X,\mathcal{F},p)\to(Y,\mathcal{G},q)</math> is a Markov kernel <math>k:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(Y,\mathcal{G})</math> such that for every measurable subset <math>B\in\mathcal{G}</math>,<ref name="krn"/>
:<math>
q(B) = \int_X k(B|x) \, p(dx) .
</math>

[[Probability spaces]] and measure-preserving Markov kernels form a [[Category (mathematics)|category]], which can be seen as the [[slice category]] <math>(\mathrm{Hom}_\mathrm{Stoch}(1,-),\mathrm{Stoch})</math>.

=== Measurable functions ===

Every measurable function <math>f:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(Y,\mathcal{G})</math> defines canonically a Markov kernel <math>\delta_f:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(Y,\mathcal{G})</math> as follows,
:<math>
\delta_f(B|x) = 1_B(f(x)) = \begin{cases}
1 & f(x)\in B ; \\
0 & f(x)\notin B
\end{cases}
</math>
for every <math>x\in X</math> and every <math>B\in\mathcal{G}</math>. This construction preserves identities and compositions, and is therefore a [[functor]] from [[category of measurable spaces|'''Meas''']] to '''Stoch'''.

=== Isomorphisms ===

By functoriality, every isomorphism of measurable spaces (in the category [[category of measurable spaces|'''Meas''']]) induces an isomorphism in '''Stoch'''. However, in '''Stoch''' there are more isomorphisms, and in particular, measurable spaces can be isomorphic in '''Stoch''' even when the underlying sets are not in bijection. 

== Relationship with other categories ==

* '''Stoch''' is the [[Kleisli category]] of the [[Giry monad]].<ref name="giry"/><ref name="fritz"/> This in particular implies that there is an [[adjunction (category theory)|adjunction]]
:<math>
\mathrm{Hom}_\mathrm{Stoch}(X,Y) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_\mathrm{Meas}(X,PY)
</math>
:between '''Stoch''' and the [[category of measurable spaces]].

* The [[left adjoint]] <math>L:\mathrm{Meas}\to\mathrm{Stoch}</math> of the adjunction above is the identity on objects, and on morphisms it gives the canonical [[Markov_kernel#Measurable_functions|Markov kernel induced by a measurable function]] described above.

* As mentioned above, one can construct a category of [[probability spaces]] and measure-preserving Markov kernels as the [[slice category]] <math>(\mathrm{Hom}_\mathrm{Stoch}(1,-),\mathrm{Stoch})</math>.

* Similarly, the [[category of probability spaces]] can be seen as the [[comma category]] <math>(\mathrm{Hom}_\mathrm{Stoch}(1,-),L)</math>. 

== Particular limits and colimits ==

Since the functor <math>L:\mathrm{Meas}\to\mathrm{Stoch}</math> is [[left adjoint]], it preserves [[colimit]]s.<ref name="riehl">{{harvp|Riehl|2016|page=140}}</ref> Because of this, all colimits in the [[category of measurable spaces]] are also colimits in '''Stoch'''. For example,

* The initial object is the empty set, with its trivial measurable structure;
* The coproduct is given by the [[disjoint union]] of measurable spaces, with its canonical [[sigma-algebra]]. 
* The sequential [[colimit]] of a decreasing [[filtration (probability theory)|filtration]] is given by the intersection of sigma-algebras.

In general, the functor <math>L</math> does not preserve [[limit (category theory)|limits]]. This in particular implies that the [[product sigma-algebra|product of measurable spaces]] is not a product in '''Stoch''' in general. Since the [[Giry monad]] is [[monoidal monad|monoidal]], however, the product of measurable spaces still makes '''Stoch''' a [[monoidal category]].<ref name="fritz" />

A limit of particular significance for [[probability theory]] is [[de Finetti's theorem]], which can be interpreted as the fact that the space of probability measures ([[Giry monad]]) is the limit in '''Stoch''' of the [[diagram (category theory)|diagram]] formed by [[exchangeability|finite permutations]] of sequences.

== Almost sure version ==

Sometimes it is useful to consider Markov kernels only up to [[almost surely|almost sure equality]], for example when talking about [[disintegration theorem|disintegrations]] or about [[regular conditional probability]].

Given [[probability spaces]] <math>(X,\mathcal{F},p)</math> and <math>(Y,\mathcal{G},q)</math>, we say that two measure-preserving kernels <math>k,h:(X,\mathcal{F},p)\to(Y,\mathcal{G},q)</math> are '''almost surely equal''' if and only if for every measurable subset <math>B\in\mathcal{G}</math>,
:<math>
k(B|x) = h(B|x)
</math>
for <math>p</math>-almost all <math>x\in X</math>.<ref name="krn"/>
This defines an [[equivalence relation]] on the set of measure-preserving Markov kernels <math>k,h:(X,\mathcal{F},p)\to(Y,\mathcal{G},q)</math>.

Probability spaces and equivalence classes of Markov kernels under the relation defined above form a [[Category (mathematics)|category]]. When restricted to [[standard Borel space|standard Borel]] probability spaces, the category is often denoted by '''Krn'''.<ref name="krn"/>
